sanskrit: कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् । क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥
hindiTranslation: हे पृथानन्दन  जो कामनाओंमें तन्मय हो रहे हैं, स्वर्गको ही श्रेष्ठ माननेवाले हैं, वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम कर्मोंमें प्रीति रखनेवाले हैं, भोगोंके सिवाय और कुछ है ही नहीं  ऐसा कहनेवाले हैं, वे अविवेकी मनुष्य इस प्रकारकी जिस पुष्पित दिखाऊ शोभायुक्त वाणीको कहा करते हैं, जो कि जन्मरूपी कर्मफलको देनेवाली है तथा भोग और ऐश्वर्यकी प्राप्तिके लिये बहुतसी क्रियाओंका वर्णन करनेवाली है ॥
englishTranslation: Those without clear seeing speak flowery words that promise birth and action-fruit, and describe many rites for enjoyment and power.
essence: Flowery promises can keep desire alive while pretending to guide you.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: People driven by desire praise rituals that promise pleasure, status, and future rewards. Their words sound attractive, but they keep the mind chasing more rewards.
simpleInsight: Not every impressive teaching frees you. Some teachings only dress up craving.
detailedMeaning: After warning about flowery promises, Krishna points to teachings that lure people toward enjoyment, status, and future reward instead of freedom.
modernRelevance: A seminar promises wealth and status if you buy the full course and follow the system. Before paying, ask the question Krishna asks: is this feeding the wanting, or calming it?
translationLiteral: कामात्मानः (those whose minds are full of desire) / स्वर्गपरा (with heaven as their highest aim) / जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् (giving the fruits of birth and action) / क्रियाविशेषबहुलाम् (full of many special rites) / भोगैश्वर्यगतिम् (a path to enjoyment and power) / प्रति (toward)
insight: Krishna's test for any teaching: does it make you want more, or want less?
